text.tspan: Page 17, Start anywhere
What the pen says, word for word, and what it means
SHOW THE BOOK, DO NOT LIST IT
“show example of this working in practice”
Reading code at the altitude you need: show it working.
WHAT WORKS, KEEP IT
“this needs to be a common theme across the
book [beside: It does not matter where you
start; it matters that you start.]”
'It does not matter where you start; it matters that you
start' runs through the whole book.
DOING STARTS EARLY, AND RUNS THROUGH
“yes but they need a place to put those
nodes & edges”
Pick a node, follow an edge: and give the reader somewhere
to put the nodes and edges.
MEET THE READER WHERE THEY ARE
“what is the context (& audience) of these
sections [over: From the register]”
What is the From the register box for, and for whom?
THE WEBSITE HOLDS WHAT THE PAGE CANNOT
“this should happen now & we should be using
prompts & QR code to examples & the text of
the prompt”
Your first graph should happen here, in chapter 3, with
prompts, the prompt's text, and QR codes to examples.
THE WEBSITE HOLDS WHAT THE PAGE CANNOT
“Question: what about if every page had a QR
code to that page (& version) online? or
section → whose visits to it will drive
revenue”
Every page, or section, could carry a QR code to itself
online, at its version, and the visits would drive
revenue.
